document_summary: Official Los Angeles Housing Department overview page describing the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO): coverage, allowable rent increases, registration, eviction grounds and relocation assistance.

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance - annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units may raise rent only once every 12 months, and only by the annual allowable rent increase percentage published by LAHD. Other increases require LAHD approval, for example capital improvement or just-and-reasonable programs.
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months, by the published allowable rent increase percentage (the percentage itself is not stated on this page). Utilities add-on removed and dependent 10% add-on removed effective 2026-02-02.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28. Includes apartments, duplexes, ADUs/JADUs and similar units. Condominiums and townhomes are not rent-regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995.
rules.exemptions: Rent may be raised to market rate if the tenant voluntarily moves out, is evicted for nonpayment or lease violation, is evicted for failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan, is evicted per a City Attorney order, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement. Luxury exemption available by application.
rules.interaction: City rent control is stricter than, and operates alongside, state rent cap law. State law is not discussed in this document.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.extraction_notes: The page does not state when the annual-increase requirement first took effect, so effective_date is null. It states changes effective 2026-02-02: no utilities percentage and no 10% for an added dependent. It also notes a historical rent freeze from 2020-03-30 through 2024-01-31. The allowable percentage is in a linked PDF not included here. The page is a secondary summary of LAMC Ch. XV, Art. 1.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO - legal grounds for eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: RSO tenants may be evicted only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD, 30-day and 60-day written notices, and payment of tenant relocation assistance. All termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: No-fault evictions require relocation assistance. Notices filed with LAHD within 3 business days of service.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (generally first built on or before October 1, 1978). Properties not covered by the RSO are subject to the separate citywide Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.interaction: The page says non-RSO properties remain subject to the City's Just Cause Ordinance. State just cause law is not discussed.

rules.extraction_notes: The page lists at-fault grounds (nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, refusal to renew a similar agreement, no reasonable access, unapproved subtenant) and no-fault grounds (owner or family move-in, resident manager, demolition or removal from the market, government order, conversion to affordable housing). It gives no relocation dollar amounts. No effective date is stated, so null. Beginning August 20, 2025 landlords must also give a Notice of Right to Counsel. Notice-filing cites are LAMC 151.09.C.9 and 165.05.B.5.
